faq_page_description: Answers about scheduled website blocking, locking rules, Resistance, categories, privacy and the free version of Ace Blocker.
faq_intro: Practical answers about network blocking, schedules, locks, categories, and Resistance.
faq_a1: Ace Blocker is a desktop website blocker for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It helps you reduce distractions using network rules, scheduled blocking, and optional locks that keep a rule in place.
faq_q2: How do I block websites at specific times?
faq_a2: Create a Network Block, select sites or categories, and set the days and hours in a weekly schedule. Ace enforces the configured rule during those periods.
faq_q3: Can I lock a blocking rule so I cannot disable it early?
faq_a3: Yes. A lock prevents you from weakening that rule until its configured lock period ends. Decide the rule and duration before activating the lock.
faq_q4: Can I block an entire category of websites?
faq_a4: Yes. Curated Categories group known websites so a single Network Block can cover a category without managing individual domains one by one.
faq_q5: What is Resistance, and is it different from blocking?
faq_a5: Resistance modifies supported websites to reduce features that encourage continued browsing, such as feeds or sidebars. You can adjust its intensity; it is not the same as blocking an entire website.
faq_q6: Does Ace Blocker collect my browsing history?
faq_a6: Ace does not collect your browsing history. Blocking decisions and statistics stay on your device. For account and subscription data, read the separate Privacy Policy.
faq_a7: Core website blocking is free. Resistance Mode requires Pro, which also unlocks all curated Categories, Custom Lists, and cloud backup.
faq_q8: Does it work beyond browser extensions?
faq_a8: Ace uses network-level blocking rather than relying only on a browser extension. Exact behavior depends on your operating system, configuration, and the type of traffic being blocked.

home_what_is_description: Ace Blocker is a desktop website blocker for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Block distracting sites with network rules, recurring schedules, and optional locks that keep your decisions in place.
home_what_is_detail: Choose individual sites or curated categories. For supported sites, Resistance tools can reduce distracting feeds and sidebars without blocking the entire destination.
home_description: Choose individual sites or entire categories. Set a weekly schedule, and lock a rule when you don't want to turn it off early.
home_decide_description: Choose what to block, when the block runs, and whether to lock the rule.
home_enforce_description: Set a weekly schedule and Ace will block those sites at the times you choose.
home_hold_title: Lock the rule when you want it to stick.
home_hold_description: Lock a rule and it cannot be weakened until the lock ends.
home_resistance_description: On supported sites, Ace can hide distracting feeds and sidebars, mute colors, or add delays. Choose a level to control the changes.
home_schedule_description: Build a week once. Ace turns those hours into active enforcement, with locks where you need the decision to stay fixed.
home_packs_title: Block a category without maintaining a domain list.
home_packs_description: Categories group known destinations so a rule can cover an entire category without maintaining a domain list by hand.
home_privacy_note: Blocking decisions and statistics stay on your device. Ace does not collect your browsing history.
home_closing_title: Make the rule before you need it.
home_closing_description: Ace is free to download. Add Pro for Resistance Mode, all Categories, Custom Lists, and backup.
policy_lock_description: This block cannot be weakened until the lock ends.
resistance_low_detail: Mild — mostly visual changes; sites stay usable.
resistance_medium_detail: Noticeable — feeds and sidebars removed, colors dulled.
resistance_high_detail: Aggressive — heavy visual changes and delays.
resistance_maximum_detail: Maximum — sites become hard or unpleasant to use.
resistance_meter_title: How much to change the site
resistance_meter_description: Higher levels hide more distracting features and can add delays on supported sites.
footer_identity_line: Block what distracts you, schedule the rule, and lock it when you want it to stick.
about_mechanism_description: It's easy to turn off a block in the moment. We built Ace so you can set rules beforehand and lock them when you want them to stay in place.
about_policy_title: Keep the whole block in one place.
about_policy_description: A Network Block brings together the sites, schedule, and lock that define one blocking rule.
about_resistance_description: Blocking is not the only lever. Ace can make supported sites less rewarding before a session turns automatic.
about_schedule_title: Time is part of the rule.
about_schedule_description: Schedules are visible rules, not background automation. You can see when blocking starts, ends, and stays locked.
about_packs_title: Start with a category, not a domain list.
about_packs_description: A Category lets one Network Block cover a curated group of related sites without maintaining every domain yourself.
